blocks.text: Jenny saw the little light beyond the window before anyone else. Flaming Head had followed their familiar energy to the new building.
Flaming Head was rising past the sill. His flame scarcely cleared his brow. He paused outside as though the last few feet had taken more effort than the whole journey used to.
Seth opened the window. Jenny stood beside him, her hand against the frame.
blocks.alt: Weakened Flaming Head arrives at the facility window as Seth and Jenny lean toward him; Billy and recovered Fist watch their reactions.

blocks.text: “What happened?”
The answer reached their minds, faint but clear. Behind them, Billy waited at the desk. Fist hovered beside his shoulder, his repaired white cuff steady. Neither could hear Flaming Head.
Seth passed the account aloud. Orkleson had built a machine to take his power. Laura had helped set the trap, then broken it to save him. She was free of her own power now.
Billy put down his pencil.
“And Orkleson?”
“Still there when he left,” Seth relayed. “The machine was wrecked.”
Flaming Head lowered himself toward the clear space inside the window. Jenny moved the curtain farther back.
For a moment they all watched the short flame tremble.
Seth went into the training room to move the practice bar out of the way.
He hooked a hand beneath it as he had that morning.
It stayed on the mat.
He changed his grip. The bar rose a little, dragged at his shoulder and came down again. Jenny caught his elbow before he tried to straighten.
“Both hands,” she said.
blocks.alt: Seth strains to lift his familiar practice bar with both hands while Jenny steadies his elbow and diminished Flaming Head watches.

blocks.text: He bent his knees, gripped it properly and lifted it clear. His arms shook as he lowered it onto the rack.
Jenny tried her usual quick dash to the operations room for water. Seth watched her cross the floor. He could follow every step, every movement of her white boots.
She stopped in the doorway and looked back at the distance she had covered.
Flaming Head hovered between them, barely lighting the edge of the mat.
Seth felt his concern before the words formed inside his mind.
“You’re weaker because I am.”
Jenny’s eyes went to the bar.
Billy came to the doorway. Seth told him, keeping one hand on the rack.
Fist drifted nearer the little flame. There was no joke this time.
“Then we look after each other,” Billy said.
Jenny returned to Seth’s side. Beyond the window, Cleveland’s lights were coming on.
Across the city, Daniel brushed brick dust from his glasses.
He had climbed through the broken warehouse window. Luke still lay on the floor beside a leaning sheet of polished metal, blond hair powdered pale with mortar.
Daniel crouched.
“Luke?”
The eyes opened.
For a moment the head stayed among the bricks. Then it lifted, slowly at first, and turned toward the sheet of metal.
Daniel stood back.
The iron jaw opened. Closed. Opened wider.
The head tilted to admire it from the side. A pleased sound rattled between the steel teeth.
blocks.alt: Inside the damaged warehouse, the newly awakened steel-jawed head delights in his reflection while a coatless Daniel watches.

blocks.text: “Luke,” Daniel said again.
“Who’s Luke?”
Daniel’s hand stopped halfway to his glasses.
The head glanced at him, then returned to the reflection. It dipped and rose, watching the empty space beneath its jaw. Instead of shrinking from it, it made another delighted turn.
“Jaws O’ Death.”
Daniel had written that name for his nephew long ago.
Now the head was pleased to claim it.
Daniel studied his face. There was no guarded look, no question about how much longer the work would take.
He let his hand fall.
“Come with me.”
Jaws followed him to the window.
Daniel climbed back onto the annex roof.
His lab coat lay in a blackened heap beside the stairhouse. Beyond it, the collector stood crooked on its trolley, glass split, control housing torn open. The copper coils were dark.
He went to the western side and touched the bent panel. All that work had ended in this.
Behind him, metal crunched.
Jaws had found a loose bracket on the roof. He bit it in two, let the pieces fall and watched them land with obvious satisfaction.
Daniel looked from the broken bracket to the torn control panel.
“Bring me that.”
He pointed to the detached metal cover beside a wheel.
Jaws caught its edge in his teeth and carried it straight over. No argument. No demand for a promise first.
Daniel took it.
Jaws rose beside his shoulder, watching his face.
“What else?”
Daniel glanced at the ruined cylinder, then at the eager iron jaws waiting beside him. Beyond the parapet, the city stretched away in rows of light.
blocks.alt: Back on the rooftop, Dork smiles beside the ruined collector while Jaws hovers eagerly at his shoulder; the scorched coat lies near the stairhouse.

blocks.text: Slowly, Daniel began to smile.
